title: Skip the Lab: Mito At-Home Test Kits
summary: Mito's new at-home test kits use the Tasso+ collector to draw a blood sample from your arm, with no needle or appointment. Seven panels, lab-run and clinician-reviewed, results in your dashboard.
body_markdown:
Table of contents


Getting your bloodwork done has always meant the same thing: book an appointment, drive to a collection site, roll up your sleeve for a phlebotomist, and hope the parking wasn’t terrible. For a lot of people, that friction is the reason a “I should really get my levels checked” thought never turns into an actual result.


We wanted to remove that friction. Today we’re launching **seven at-home test kits** you can order online, collect from your own kitchen table, and mail back, with the same lab analysis, clinician review, and dashboard you’d get from a full Mito panel.


## No needle, no finger stick


The kits use the **Tasso+ collector** , a small single-use device that sits on your upper arm. You press it into place, a tiny puncture and a gentle vacuum draw a capillary blood sample, and you’re done in a few minutes. There’s no venipuncture, no vial, and no repeated finger-pricking. You use just one painless collector and a sample container.


Every kit ships with everything you need:


- The single-use Tasso+ collector
- Collection materials and a sample tube
- Step-by-step instructions
- Prepaid return packaging (both directions)


Once you’ve collected your sample, you drop it in the prepaid mailer and send it back to the lab. Your results post straight to your **Mito dashboard** as soon as the lab finishes, reviewed by a clinician. It is the same experience as our in-lab panels, minus the trip.

## How the process works, start to finish


1. **Order online.** Pick your kit and check out. Members see at-cost pricing automatically.
2. **Kit ships to you.** Expect it in about **2–5 business days** via FedEx. You can track it from your dashboard.
3. **Collect your sample.** Follow the instructions, use the Tasso+ collector on your upper arm, and fill in the collection form. Take a minute to double-check your name and date of birth match your order. The lab needs those to line up.
4. **Send it back.** Drop the prepaid return package at a FedEx location the same day you collect. Samples travel back to the lab quickly and stay stable for several days in transit, so a same-day FedEx handoff is well within range.
5. **Get clinician-reviewed results.** Your numbers post to your Mito dashboard once the lab completes testing, with plain-language context and next steps.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**How soon should I collect after the kit arrives?** Collect and mail it back promptly. The sample is designed to stay stable in transit, and the prepaid return shipping is expedited so it reaches the lab quickly.


**Where do I find tracking?** Both the outbound and return shipments are visible in your dashboard.


**What if my kit arrives damaged?** Don’t use it. Reach out to support and we’ll get a replacement sent.


**Can I cancel after ordering?** There’s a short window to change or cancel before a kit is fulfilled. Once it ships, it’s on its way to you.


**Why does my info need to match exactly?** The lab matches your sample to your order using the details on your collection form. Small things like a nickname or a typo are usually fine, but if your information can’t be confidently matched, the lab may not be able to run the sample, so accurate details protect your result.


## One important note


These seven kits are Mito’s self-collection option: the kit is shipped to you, you use the Tasso+ collector yourself, and no phlebotomist visits. Mito also offers a separate[professional at-home blood draw service](https://mitohealth.com/guide/at-home-blood-draw) for eligible standard lab orders. With that service, a licensed phlebotomist comes to your home and performs a venous blood draw. Collection-site appointments remain available for standard lab orders. Scans and fitness tests, including[DEXA body composition](https://mitohealth.com/products/dexa-body-composition-scan) and[DEXA bone density](https://mitohealth.com/products/dexa-bone-density-scan) scans, the[coronary artery calcium scan](https://mitohealth.com/products/coronary-artery-calcium-cac-scan) ,[VO2 Max](https://mitohealth.com/products/vo2-max) and[resting metabolic rate (RMR)](https://mitohealth.com/products/resting-metabolic-rate-rmr) tests, and the[full-body MRI](https://mitohealth.com/products/prenuvo-full-body-mri-scan) , are booked at partner testing and imaging centers.


The seven at-home kits and professional at-home blood draws both remain available. Neither replaces the other. The kits are a lower-friction way to check the things that benefit from regular tracking, or to get started before you commit to a full panel.
